checks.claim: Morgan Stanley has 5GW pushed into 2029, making 2028 net adds flat
sources: BigGo Finance on the MS note, 2026-11-08
checks.text: Morgan Stanley (2026-11-08/09) moved ~5GW of US data-center IT load from 2028 into 2029, about 20% of the 2028 slate. It now models 19.9GW of 2028 additions vs 27.6GW in 2029, which leaves 2028 flat vs 2027 (about −4% y/y). MS calls these postponements, not cancellations, with 2027 unchanged.

checks.claim: This could be a problem for all bottleneck companies
sources: BigGo Finance on the MS note
checks.text: MS itself flags a possible temporary 2028 slowdown, with upstream suppliers facing slower orders, rising inventories and margin pressure. Offsets: Bernstein sees only a 2–4% realistic US capacity hit; SemiAnalysis says ~75% of 2027 capacity in the top 20 states is already under construction.

tenets.claim: Post-midterm politics is getting more difficult for US data centers (TX/OH/GA/PA governors, the Texas permit freeze, stricter large-load tariffs). The Street models a 2028 GW ramp; some of it is already moving into 2029, which would leave 2028 net adds flat and hit every bottleneck supplier priced for that ramp.

checks.claim: Anthropic's acceleration is not enough for combined ARR to justify the return on spend
checks.text: SRS calc on the deck's own model. Combined ARR is ~$130bn today: Anthropic above $80bn in October plus OpenAI ~$50bn in September. At ~$15bn/month of combined net new ARR (Anthropic ~$8bn in October, OpenAI ~+70% q/q in Q3), the labs exit 2026 at ~$165–175bn vs the model's $195bn. Reaching $452bn in 2027 needs ~$21bn/month all year. Anthropic is back at its Jun–Jul pace, but that alone does not close the gap.

checks.claim: He lied to the board about how much Megaspeed actually shipped
checks.text: No report says this. Reported so far: the board opened an independent investigation on 2026-11-08. The Business Times reports a ~50,000-unit gap between Nvidia's initial accounting to US officials of hardware supplied to Megaspeed and Bloomberg's customs data (~136k GPUs, ≥$4.6bn, 2023–Nov-25). The Information reports ≥$7.5bn / ~240k GPUs moved into China through a linked network, which Reuters could not verify. Fortune says the probe 'could look at' questionable public statements. The reported gap concerns statements to US officials, not the board.

An SRS inference, not a datapoint. The nearest reported item runs the other way: Nvidia itself is reportedly cutting neocloud Vera Rubin allocations by up to 50% and reallocating to SpaceX (SB #65967).
